---
title: "Shared-file stores on GitHub"
---

This is an unmerged experimental source candidate, not an installed feature yet.

The existing ordinary GitHub backups keep one ZIP per folder or version.
A complete CAS store is different: each distinct whole file is stored once, and
small directory/version records identify which files belong together. CAS means
content-addressed storage: file contents determine their identifiers. Xet instead
can share smaller pieces within files. Neither changes your analysis source paths.

This new library slice packages the complete existing CAS store as a ZIP for one
long-running GitHub storage release. It preserves existing file hashes, tree
identifiers and legacy readers. It does not convert or migrate local archives.
Configured build/restore wiring is the next separate slice.

## What is verified before a reference can be saved

Export holds the cooperative store writer claim while copying. It excludes
coordination state, then checks every copied file, every content-addressed object
including orphan objects, directory identities and each tree, flat-catalogue or
legacy snapshot. Complete metadata must be present in the exported store.
Project-only metadata is not silently invented or copied from another project.

The ZIP has a bounded, versioned file-membership/length/digest envelope. Import
first checks the trusted external ZIP digest and length, uses the existing
traversal/link/duplicate/expansion guards, and then deeply checks the whole store
in a fresh private location. The envelope is removed after checking so that new
versions can be added and the store exported again.

A checksum inside the ZIP alone does not authenticate it. Keep the exact store
reference, including ZIP digest, in trusted project Git history.

## GitHub transfer and failure behavior

A new immutable ZIP is uploaded, then downloaded and independently checked before
the library returns a reference eligible for project commit. A failed upload or
verification leaves the previous good asset/reference intact; an unreferenced new
ZIP can remain. Same-name retries accept only independently verified exact bytes.
No delete-old-before-upload replacement or automatic retention cleanup is used.

Recovery downloads the selected complete ZIP and uses the ordinary local CAS
readers. It needs no Xet engine or Hugging Face account. Current library tests use
only disposable synthetic files and a loopback mocked REST service, not live
GitHub archives. Real GitHub validation and configured command examples remain
pending. No multi-project/shared-store namespace, distributed linear-head merge,
hot-copy or power-loss guarantee is introduced.

All existing ordinary latest/archive paths and metadata ZIPs remain unchanged.

The claim is cooperative: not every low-level existing tree writer acquires it. Stop all store writers before export. The tests cover busy-claim rejection; this is not a safe concurrent hot-copy mechanism. New acceptance also exercises all four flat encodings with direct version references, original legacy flat snapshots without the project ledger, missing objects and unknown catalogue files.
